Title: Thoughts Betrayed: New Wordings Compilations (Repost and Update)

Messages.Author: The Corrupter
Messages.Body:
Much of the following has already been posted. Any opinions regarding
them are happily encouraged.

---

I'm starting this thread to organize all of the ideas seen regarding
possible new wordings of Thoughts Betrayed. I apologize for not
remembering who came up with them. Whether or not Thoughts Betrayed
works as is or as follows is up to you. (Apologies for some bad wordings...)

Template: Thoughts Betrayed, Dominate Combat Card...
In all cases, Thoughts betrayed is played at the beginning of
combat, unless otherwise noted.

v1) Cost: 2
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of every round.
Superior: Opposing Minion cannot play combat cards this combat.
Basic Effect: As official card text, except the inferior is given
some teeth.

v2) Cost: 0
Inferior: At the end of every round, this minion may spend 1 blood to
cause one damage to the opposing minion.
Superior: For the remainder of this combat, this minion may spend 1
blood to cancel the opposing minion from playing a combat card.
Basic Effect: Canceling multiple cards costs more, while lower
abilities (the inferior) become useful.

v3) Cost: 2
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of every round.
Superior: The opposing minion cannot play combat cards this round.
Basic Effect: Gives the inferior some power, and makes the superior a
method to get to second round combat alive.

v4) Cost: 2
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of every round.
Superior: No combat cards can be played by combatants this combat.
Basic Effect: Gives the inferior some power, and makes the superior a
purely defensive card or a permanent-based combat card.

v5) Cost: 2
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of every round.
Superior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage for every combat card
played this combat.
Basic Effect: Gives the inferior some power, and makes combat decks
scared to use their combat powers in the superior, without totally
curtailing their power.

v6) Cost: 2
Only usable by a vampire which has just successfully blocked an action.
Inferior: Opposing Minino suffers one damage at the end of every round.
Superior: Opposing Minion cannot play combat cards this combat.
Basic Effect: Makes the card only usable in defense (blocking), makes
the inferior useful, but basicly keeps the card the same.

v7) Cost: 2
Inferior: Play before range is determined. Opposing minion takes an
additional 1 damage in the first round of combat during strike resolution.
Superior: Play before range is determined. Opposing minion cannot {play}
any cards for the remainder of combat once range is being determined.
Basic Effect: Keeps card text mostly the same, but allows the
opponents to play _some_ cards that still make them a threat while still
giving the vampire playing Thoughts Betrayed a huge power.
(opponent can play cards up until pre-range ends on this round. Think
Wolf Claws, etc...)

v8) Cost: 3
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of this round.
Superior: Opposing Minion cannot play combat cards this combat.
Basic Effect: Makes the cost more of a detriment.

v9) Cost: 2
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of this round.
Superior: Opposing Minion cannot play strike or strike-modifying
cards this combat.
Basic Effect: Allows the opponent some combat defense but takes away
most of their power.

v10) Cost: 0
Inferior: Play this card to burn a combat card other than a Thoughts
Betrayed played by a minion the vampire is in combat with. Do not replace
until after combat.
Superior: As above but the Opposing Minion may not replace the card
burned until after combat.
Basic Effect: Limits key offensive/defensive measures of opponent,
but doesn't kill opponents ability to respond.

v11) Cost: 2
Inferior: Opposing Minion suffers one damage at the end of each round.
Superior: Opposing Minion cannot replace cards used in combat, and
cannot play a card of the same name as one already played that combat.
Basic effect: Gives the inferior some use, and the superior limits
but does not totally hose combat from the opponent.

Comments?

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
> In general, I feel uncomfortable with any card that says "opponent may not
> play *any* card" for any significant length of time. No matter what the
> cost, it basically becomes a "go get a Coke" card, as James Hamblin
> complained.

Woohoo! I've coined a term! Go me!

Ahem. Sorry.

> In addition, such effects are unprecedented in Jyhad: the
> best you can get from the original set is not allowing one particular type
> of card for one round.

So let's make a list;

Immortal Grapple: Prevents non-hand strikes, and maneuvers (but only
after the first round)
Blood Rage/Fury: Prevents Fortitude prevention and equipment
Drawing out the Beast: Prevents maneuvers, equipment
Hidden Lurker/Fast Reaction: Prevents strikes for first round
Dog Pack: Prevents S:CE
S:CE: Prevents strikes

I'm sure that there are more; these stand out in my mind. All of these
are quite powerful, but TB is more so.

> I think Thoughts betrayed should be along the lines of:
>
> Cost 2 blood
>
> normal: Opponent may not Maneuver in this combat.
> Superior: Opponent may not Maneuver or press in this combat.
>
> This is still a hellacious combat card in Tremere or Giovanni deck, with
> defensive applications for gun decks.

I think that a better (and certainly not as hallacious) version would
be:

Cost: 2 blood
Inf: Play before range is chosen in the first round of combat. Opposing
minion may only play maneuvers to cancel maneuvers and may only press to
continue combat.
Sup: As above, but opposing minion may not play strikes which do not
cause damage during this combat.

I think this is a wording that hasn't been come up with before. It
doesn't screw combat decks, it gives the Tremere more of a chance to get
into the second round, and it prevents S:CE, albeit at a cost.

> I'm aware that TB would no longer hose S:CE, which is presumably one of
> its original design goals. However, S:CE is a general problem, not one
> experience only by Dominate clans. If S:CE must be addressed via a hoser
> card, the card should be disciplineless.

How about this:

Evocation of Rage
Cost: 0.
Play before strike declaration once range has been determined as short.
Opposing minion may not play non-damaging strikes and gets +1 hand
damage for the remainder of combat. This minion has an optional press,
only usable to continue combat.

What do you think?

James

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
In general, I feel uncomfortable with any card that says "opponent may not
play *any* card" for any significant length of time. No matter what the
cost, it basically becomes a "go get a Coke" card, as James Hamblin

complained. In addition, such effects are unprecedented in Jyhad: the

best you can get from the original set is not allowing one particular type
of card for one round.

I think Thoughts betrayed should be along the lines of:

Cost 2 blood

normal: Opponent may not Maneuver in this combat.
Superior: Opponent may not Maneuver or press in this combat.

This is still a hellacious combat card in Tremere or Giovanni deck, with
defensive applications for gun decks.

I'm aware that TB would no longer hose S:CE, which is presumably one of

its original design goals. However, S:CE is a general problem, not one
experience only by Dominate clans. If S:CE must be addressed via a hoser
card, the card should be disciplineless.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: Scott Whittaker
Messages.Body:
Your list, describing exactly what type of cards are forbidden (or
rendered ineffective, if you prefer) by these original Jyhad cards
should be revised slightly, in that Immortal Grapple works right from
the outset (not just the second round). Secondly, on the matter of Blood
Rage and Blood Fury, it raises the question of whether or not Chimestry
should be able to soak these Thaumaturgical rituals.
Scott Whittaker

combat.
Superior: As above, and opponent may not replace cards used in
combat until the end of combat.

Messages.Author: Ben Redmond
Messages.Body:
concerning Thoughts betrayed (TB). In our gaming group we
have decided, like others, I assume, to ban this card. The
reasoning is purely and simply that it has no possible
counter - similarily we are debating (well okay, arguing),
over whether to similarily ban blood to water. However,
whereas most of the players in my gaming group say that you
can't change a card at all - it stays as read (or as
officially errata'd) or it goes, I, on the other hand, would
like to see cards changed slightly so that they can still be
played (perhaps some what selfishely as I have a Ventrue deck
that I attempt to fight with, and TB would be a great adition
to it). I personally would favour the version that is similar
to hidden lurker(HL) / fast reaction(FR) (2 blood and a
superior discipline required makes up for a HL/FR that can be
used on any combat - perhaps for the whole combat, perhaps
for just the one round. However, this is very preventable
with fortitude combat, which had become very powerful in the
Ancient Hearts suppliment (Kiss of Ra, extra damage
prevention card - Hidden strength <note: this is mainly worth
while in a card limit environment>) especially when linked
with protean and animalism as is most commonly found.
However, it is probably best to leave this to other cards and
so the HL/FR version seems most appropriate. I think that my
main moan about fortitude stems from the fact that my Brujah
can't beat up the gangrel, but the gangrel can beat up my
brujah - I dont want to have to leave it all to the Assamites
and the Tremere (and having card limits maked the assamites a
bit rubbish at it anyway.)

Ben

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
(hey, are you the Kristopher Zeirhut who graduated from Cornell a few
years ago?)

Kristopher Zeirhut wrote:
"All you whiners about thoughts betrayed are just not being creative.
Want a one-card hose against
thoughts betrayed, how about shadow of the beast? (new in V;TES), it give
a free maneuver and press every combat. In addition, thoughts betrayed
helps to deal with the combat ends cheese."

TB is considered a broken card because it goes completley against the
theory of the game. It is a Trump card, and one of the very few in the
game, if not the only one in the game (well, AI springs to mind...:-).
Jyhad does not and should not rely on such Trump cards, and thus has no
need for TB. It's effect is completely inequivelant to it's cost (2
blood), prevents your opponent from playing the game (and makes them go
get a coke...), and is unwarented in the structure of the game.

No other card has the ability to completely destroy the opponents ability
to act in so many ways. No other card screws everything. Jyhad is a big
and complex game of Paper-Sciscors-Rock, and all other cards are either a
Paper, a Scisor, or a Rock. TB functions as a Bomb, if you are farmilliar
with the P-S-R variant rules :-).

As to the "Single Card Hose" against TB (which isn't desiarable in the
first place), oh good. Shadow of the Beast allows you to move to long
range from the Tremere while he steals your blood, and then allows you to
cycle an extra press out of his hand while he presses into the second
round and burns you, while you stand around and twiddle your thumbs.

As the Corrupter stated, there are plenty of ways to deal with S:CE that
do not prevent them from playing the game. Immortal Grapple. Hidden
Lurker. Fast Reaction. Psyche. Dog Pack. I am fairly certain that
every single clan now has a way to deal with S:CE, one way or the other,
without TB. Without TB, your opponent can still try. With TB, your
opponent does not even have that choice.
